title: Where a position split could come from
checkpoint: Immediately after the nonfading upper SSL warp is accepted, still in Area 1, before the disappearing action.

records.display: MarioObject.header.gfx.pos: the stored display vector read by the retry

verdict: Whole-game source catalog with checked finite exclusions; not an exhaustive live-writer or no-Ink theorem.

situations.title: Walking, falling and the ordinary position copies
situations.status: Insufficient at ground copy · other checkpoints open
situations.effect: Mario takes a step, so his movement position changes. The action usually updates his display next, and Mario's object update later copies the movement position into the collision record. In between, the numbers can disagree.
situations.prerequisite: This is the everyday machinery behind walking, sliding, falling and airborne actions.
situations.area1: Yes. SSL uses it too. Whether Mario can enter a particular airborne action without a new A press is a separate problem.
situations.timing: The warp gets checked before the ordinary action loop. A step taken later in that update is too late to explain a gap that was already there when the warp accepted Mario.
situations.evidence: We have the update order and proofs for particular copies and movement steps. That gives us useful stopping points.
situations.missing: Follow the earlier action to its last copy. A big speed value alone does not move Mario between two arbitrary checks.

gap.amount: 0 at the completed ground copy; air/water copies reviewed separately
gap.verdict: Insufficient — already proved at the completed ground copy
gap.detail: A step may briefly leave the old display behind. The completed ground, air or water copy replaces it with the new movement position. Later shell, water and sand adjustments are counted in their own rows.
gap.limit: This is not a bound on every intermediate displacement or a proof that every action takes one of these completed copies.
gap.basis: InkPostDialogGroundReset.v: completed ground-copy result; other movement copies remain separately scoped

insufficiency.scope: At the completed actual US/JP ground-step display copy, with the reached Mario pointer, readable movement Y, a valid Object-pool slot and separate MarioState storage, display Y equals movement Y. The whole ground-call theorem supplies this copy checkpoint. This does not cover an earlier retry, every action, or later offset and position writes.

review.summary: The completed ground copy supplies zero gap, already proved. Do not reopen that checkpoint merely because other actions exist.

situations.title: The floor check borrows Mario's display position
situations.status: Helper · needs an earlier height gap
situations.effect: First, wall correction can move Mario's movement position. Then the game looks for a floor. If it finds nothing, it copies the stored display position into movement and tries again. The collision record can still be back where it started.
situations.prerequisite: No special enemy is needed. This is part of Mario's normal preparation before interactions.
situations.area1: Yes. This is what makes the supplied SSL Ink setup work. We still need gameplay to supply the low collision position and high display together.
situations.timing: The retry happens before the warp interaction. So movement and display can agree up high while the collision record still touches the warp down below.
situations.evidence: The real copy and second-query connection are proved. We also have a successful supplied JP setup and a checked floor-list certificate. The supplied starting gap is doing real work in that demonstration.
situations.missing: Create the first floor miss, useful display height, low warp contact and correctly timed top in one legal continuation.

gap.amount: 0 between display and movement after retry
gap.verdict: Consumes a gap; does not create the raised display
gap.detail: The retry can turn low movement into high movement by copying the display. It can leave the collision record low, which is exactly why the supplied setup works. Wall correction is a separate X/Z change, not a new upward display offset.
gap.limit: The useful display-versus-collision gap and first missing floor must already be available. Live correction and floor choice still matter.

review.summary: This is the consumer that makes the supplied Ink setup useful. It needs the earlier raised display; it does not manufacture it.

situations.title: The floor moves Mario, but does the display follow?
situations.effect: Floor alignment can set Mario's movement height to the remembered floor height without itself replacing his stored display. Animation movement can also change his movement coordinates.
situations.prerequisite: A ground action, an animation that moves Mario, or a change in the support beneath him.
situations.area1: Yes. These are ordinary helpers. What we do not have is the large, surviving mismatch needed for Ink.
situations.timing: Most of this happens during the action. We must keep reading past the interesting assignment: a later copy might immediately remove the advantage.
situations.evidence: The existing ground-reset and alignment proofs settle their stated cases. They do not cover every possible earlier action and remembered floor.
situations.missing: Find a mismatch that survives the following copies and reaches the next useful floor retry, or rule out that particular sequence.

gap.amount: Old display Y − remembered floor Y; animation depends on its signed translation
gap.verdict: A possible downward writer; useful size is still unproved
gap.detail: Floor alignment writes the remembered floor height into actual Y while leaving the stored display alone at that assignment. A lower remembered floor could therefore create an upward gap. Animation translation instead adds a selected signed translation to movement; a negative Y translation could lower it.
gap.limit: No controller-reachable large mismatch or useful animation frame/flag sequence is supplied. Later copies and the matrix helper still need their actual effects checked. There is no justified route-wide maximum yet.

review.summary: Check a reached downward floor snap or animation translation, then the next display copy. A useful retained size has not been bounded.

situations.title: Ride a platform while the other positions stay put
situations.effect: A moving platform can carry Mario's movement position while his display and collision positions stay put for that entire platform phase.
situations.prerequisite: Mario must actually have a valid remembered platform. Merely being near a moving object is not enough.
situations.area1: Yes. SSL has Tox Boxes and the pyramid top. Getting useful support from one at the right time still needs an explanation.
situations.timing: This happens before Mario's next update. The support check can erase the remembered platform, and moving Mario here does not move the collision record used for warp contact.
situations.evidence: The complete US/JP platform phase preserves display and collision under the stated normal Object-pool conditions. A missing or too-distant floor also provably clears the remembered platform.
situations.missing: Explain how the collision record was already low while Mario still had useful support and a high display. Platform movement alone does not supply all three.

gap.amount: Old display-minus-movement gap − platform vertical displacement
gap.verdict: Can change one gap, but keeps the collision record where it was
gap.detail: A downward ride can make display sit above actual Mario. The complete platform phase preserves both display and raw collision coordinates. Starting with all three together therefore does not create the required high-display/low-collision pair during that phase.
gap.limit: A later collision copy could make collision low only if display survives until then. Live downward displacement, remembered support and those later copies are separate obligations; no maximum useful drop is established.

review.summary: A downward support move can separate movement from display. Collision stays with display during the proved platform phase, so another copy must complete the useful pair.

situations.title: Chuckya and King Bob-omb: the stock lists cannot choose them
situations.effect: While Mario is held, the shared anchor can place his stored display at the anchor's raw position, including its graphical Y offset. When he is thrown, the grabbed action can copy that display position back into movement.
situations.prerequisite: A Chuckya or King Bob-omb parent has to create and run the anchor.
situations.area1: The checked Area-1 regular, macro and special spawn lists choose neither parent. Loading a model does not put that enemy in the level.
situations.timing: This really changes the stored display. It is more than a funny animation or a launch-speed change.
situations.evidence: Coq checks both parents, their shared anchor chain and their absence from the stock lists in US and JP. The generated C bodies also have no direct parent reference.
situations.missing: This stock-list explanation is finished. A different proposal would have to show how legal gameplay creates the missing actor; that broader creation history is still open.

proof.claim: The checked stock Area-1 lists cannot select Chuckya or King Bob-omb.
proof.scope: Both US and JP; regular script choices and the checked Area-1 macro and special-object lists. This excludes these stock selections, not every possible later object-creation history.

situations.title: Dorrie: no neck lift from the stock SSL lists
situations.effect: Dorrie's neck lift sets Mario's movement position using his collision position and the movement of Dorrie's head.
situations.prerequisite: A live Dorrie running the head-lift behavior.
situations.area1: The stock SSL lists checked here cannot choose Dorrie.
situations.timing: This is a special movement helper, separate from the ordinary platform ride.
situations.evidence: Both versions have a checked Dorrie exclusion. His head lift is also one of exactly three direct callers of the movement-position setter in the generated code.
situations.missing: The stock-list case is done. Bringing a Dorrie or a useful gap from elsewhere would require a real creation or transition sequence; we have not granted one.

proof.claim: The checked stock SSL lists cannot select Dorrie.
proof.scope: Both US and JP; regular script choices and the checked Area-1 macro and special-object lists. This excludes these stock selections, not every possible later object-creation history.

situations.title: Those other pyramids are not SSL's pyramid top
situations.effect: The tilting platforms in LLL and BitFS use a special rider correction that sets Mario's movement position.
situations.prerequisite: One of those two tilting-platform behaviors.
situations.area1: Neither behavior is selected by the checked stock SSL lists. SSL's exploding pyramid top is a different object with different code.
situations.timing: Two objects looking like pyramids does not give them the same movement helper.
situations.evidence: Coq excludes both stock selections in US and JP. Their shared callback is another of the three direct movement-setter callers.
situations.missing: The stock-list proposal is ruled out. A different legal way of creating or importing the behavior would need its own demonstration.

proof.claim: The checked stock SSL lists cannot select either LLL or BitFS tilting-pyramid behavior.
proof.scope: Both US and JP; regular script choices and the checked Area-1 macro and special-object lists. This excludes these stock selections, not every possible later object-creation history.

situations.title: Hoot: the stock SSL lists cannot supply the ride
situations.effect: While Mario rides Hoot, the action places his movement position below Hoot and then copies it into display.
situations.prerequisite: Hoot must exist, Mario must grab him, and the riding action must still be active.
situations.area1: The checked stock SSL lists never choose Hoot.
situations.timing: Even with an owl, an intermediate mismatch is only useful if it survives the action's own display copy.
situations.evidence: The US/JP stock-list exclusion is proved. The riding code shows where the position change and copy occur.
situations.missing: The normal stock-spawn explanation is finished. A claim about every possible action history would also need to show that the riding action cannot begin without its proper actor.

proof.claim: The checked stock SSL lists cannot select Hoot.
proof.scope: Both US and JP; regular script choices and the checked Area-1 macro and special-object lists. This excludes these stock selections, not every possible later object-creation history.

situations.title: The palm tree can push one position
situations.status: Helper · needs an earlier height gap
situations.effect: The push helpers can change Mario's movement X/Z without directly changing his collision or display coordinates.
situations.prerequisite: A tree/pole callback or an object interaction that actually reaches the push helper.
situations.area1: Yes. The palm tree at (-5989,0,-4850) is there in the stock level. Other solid objects and enemies also use push logic.
situations.timing: The tree's callback runs after collision detection and before Mario's update. Interaction pushes have to fit their own place in the handler order.
situations.evidence: We have a source proof of this position-writing path. So 'none of the object callbacks can move Mario' would be false. The new stock-list check also correctly finds the tree.
situations.missing: Follow a real push through wall correction, the floor query and the next copies. The tree being far from the warp does not by itself prove that every possible sequence fails.

gap.amount: 0 new vertical gap from the direct push writes
gap.verdict: A sideways helper, not the height source
gap.detail: These helpers write X/Z. They could matter by changing the next floor query while a raised display already exists. The tree push scales its raw horizontal offset by (radius − distance) / radius; the interaction push aims at the combined hitbox radius and padding.
gap.limit: Do not assign a reachable horizontal maximum without the real actor sizes and input positions. Calls through the wall/floor helpers need their own connection.

review.summary: The direct writes are sideways. They may help lose a floor, but an independent height producer must already exist.

situations.title: Bounces and knockback are different kinds of help
situations.effect: A bounce can put Mario's movement height at the top of an object's hitbox. Other hits first change his speed or action, leaving later movement to do the actual moving.
situations.prerequisite: The relevant enemy, hazard and interaction. A Goomba bounce and a gust of wind do not write the same things.
situations.area1: SSL has several of these enemies and hazards. Their presence does not automatically give us a useful position split.
situations.timing: Most of these handlers come after the warp handler. Once the nonfading warp accepts Mario, the loop stops; we cannot sneak an extra bounce in afterward in that same loop.
situations.evidence: The handler order and bounce write are in the actual source. The accepted-warp proof and replay cover their stated path, not every earlier bounce.
situations.missing: Pick an earlier interaction that can really occur, then follow its action change and all the position copies before the warp.

gap.amount: Old display Y − (object Y + hitbox height)
gap.verdict: A real height assignment; no useful large gap demonstrated
gap.detail: The bounce helper snaps actual Mario to the hitbox top. Depending on the incoming position, that could move him up or down. Damage, tornado capture and wind primarily set speed or action; speed by itself is not a position gap.
gap.limit: We have not bounded the reached SSL bounce placements and incoming split. The warp handler runs earlier, and an accepted warp stops the loop. No numeric route-wide maximum is claimed.

review.summary: The hitbox-top snap changes actual Y. We still need a reachable SSL incoming pose with a large enough downward change and a surviving display.

situations.title: Heave-Ho, bullies and Bowser's shockwave are off these lists
situations.effect: These actors do different jobs. Heave-Ho supplies launch speed and status, not Chuckya's display anchor. Bullies can adjust movement height. Shockwave bouncing moves Mario and then updates display.
situations.prerequisite: The matching actor and a legitimate interaction or action.
situations.area1: The checked stock lists do not select Heave-Ho, the five named bully variants or BowserShockWave.
situations.timing: A speed change is not an immediate position change. We cannot replace all seven behaviors with a generic 'enemy moves Mario' assumption.
situations.evidence: The absence of all seven named behavior choices is proved in both generated versions.
situations.missing: Their stock-list paths are ruled out. A broader exclusion still needs proper actor creation and action history; these checks do not let us invent either.

proof.claim: The checked stock SSL lists cannot select Heave-Ho, the five named bully variants or BowserShockWave.
proof.scope: Both US and JP; regular script choices and the checked Area-1 macro and special-object lists. This excludes these stock selections, not every possible later object-creation history.

situations.title: Trees, ledges and hanging points
situations.effect: These actions attach Mario's movement position to something, or move it along an animation. Usually a display copy follows.
situations.prerequisite: A climbable tree/pole, a ledge or a hangable surface, plus the action that uses it.
situations.area1: There is no stock pole beside the pyramid-top warp. The palm tree at (-5989,0,-4850) uses pole actions, far from the warp at (-2048,768,-1024). The two regular poles are in Area 2. The checked Area-1 static mesh and pyramid top have no hangable triangles; Area 2 has six. Ordinary Area-1 ledges remain relevant.
situations.timing: A gap halfway through an action may be gone before the next warp check. The exit from the attachment matters as much as the attachment itself.
situations.evidence: The source identifies the pole, ledge and hanging writers. Our local proofs do not yet classify every way of entering and leaving those actions.
situations.missing: The absent local pole cannot supply a release right at the warp. A remote tree exit, a different ledge history or a later dynamic attachment would need its own producer and transfer; the stock-data check does not close all such histories.

gap.amount: Pole/hang copies: 0. Ledge release: a 100-unit subtraction or a shallower floor snap
gap.verdict: Insufficient at the local drop — source review
gap.detail: Letting go of a ledge shifts X/Z back by a nominal 60 and lowers Y by the source's 100-unit cap, before setting soft bonk. From a synchronized pose at ordinary heights this gives at most about +100 of vertical gap at that local write. Pole placement and stationary hanging subsequently copy movement to display.
gap.limit: The ledge number is source arithmetic at the drop, not a proof that the gap survives the resumed action. It is short of 1,170.864868 by itself. Live attachment exits remain separate.
gap.basis: Pinned stock area/helper/tree/mesh checks in split_catalog.py; action source review; no full exit-history proof

review.summary: No pole beside the Area-1 top warp. The distant palm tree uses pole actions, whose normal placement copies the display. A local ledge release is only a nominal 100-unit drop; neither is an established source of the supplied gap.

situations.title: The cannon really can leave the display behind
situations.status: Needs A to fire · other exits open
situations.effect: While Mario enters and sits in the cannon, the action updates his movement position and copies it to display. Firing moves him 120 units along the aim and returns before that display copy. That can leave the old display behind.
situations.prerequisite: An opened cannon and an actual cannon-entry interaction.
situations.area1: Yes. The cannon is at (6863,0,-6860), and the stock Bob-omb Buddy can open it.
situations.timing: Here is the restriction: the normal firing branch tests INPUT_A_PRESSED. Sitting in the cannon takes the ordinary display-copy path. Invisibility alone does not preserve a useful high display.
situations.evidence: This comes from the actual cannon code, including its early return. Coq separately confirms the stock cannon selection. We have not presented the firing observation as a proved universal action-history exclusion.
situations.missing: A no-new-A proposal needs a legal exit or interruption with a useful remaining gap. Normal firing does not meet the button rule.

gap.amount: 0 while seated; firing leaves display at or below movement
gap.verdict: Insufficient at normal launch — source and finite checks
gap.detail: Firing moves actual Mario 120 units along the aim before the usual display copy. The clamped pitch is nonnegative: the checked sine-table expression raises actual Y by 0 to 118.169815 units. Starting synchronized, display-minus-movement Y is therefore nonpositive at those writes.
gap.limit: The normal firing branch also requires INPUT_A_PRESSED. The finite pitch calculation does not prove controller history, later sound-call effects or a warp transfer.

review.summary: Normal launch needs an A edge and moves actual Mario upward, leaving the wrong sign of gap. An unusual exit would be a separate claim.

situations.title: A Tweester can move Mario, but it also updates the display
situations.status: Insufficient at normal copy · other checkpoints open
situations.effect: The tornado action moves Mario around the tornado and updates his stored display.
situations.prerequisite: A real tornado interaction and the tornado-twirling action.
situations.area1: Yes. SSL has Tweesters. The checked stock selections confirm this.
situations.timing: Tornado capture is after warp in the interaction list, and the twirling movement occurs during the action. Those placements limit when it could help.
situations.evidence: The generated US/JP continuation after the early ejection test now has a completed-copy proof. Both floor outcomes reach equal movement/display Y at that checkpoint, excluding the supplied low-State/high-display pair there. A new finite US/JP transport diagnostic tests 188,416 prescribed home-boundary schedules per version, stopping at first hitbox overlap or hiding. None reaches useful warp proximity. A separate relaxed-steering ledge pose can geometrically overlap Mario at the supplied low contact point; it is not an oscillation route.
situations.missing: Find an actual controller-driven oscillation route that avoids unwanted capture and hiding. The tested fixed-ray schedules do not supply one. The conditional western-ledge contact grants the two poses and scale phase, and creates no gap. The ordinary ejection source continues into an air step with another display copy; exceptional interruptions and later writers still need their own proof. Warp acceptance is checked before tornado capture, so a lift from the same accepted contact is too late.

gap.amount: 0 at the completed non-ejecting display-copy checkpoint
gap.verdict: Insufficient — already proved at the normal Tweester copy
gap.detail: Both floor-found and floor-missing branches feed into the same real display copy. The new US/JP proof follows that actual continuation and completed callee: display Y and movement Y are equal there, however far the Tweester just moved Mario.
gap.limit: The theorem starts after the early ejection test and ends at the completed copy. The following angle call and surrounding action history remain outside it. Separate source review follows ordinary ejection into an air step with another display copy, conditional on retaining that action and avoiding common cancellations; this is not a new complete Clight proof. Moving the Tweester itself does not bypass either copy.

insufficiency.scope: At the completed actual US/JP non-ejecting display copy, under its stated storage conditions, the supplied low-movement/high-display pair is impossible. Both floor-query outcomes are covered. Ejection, the following angle call and other later writers remain outside this result.

review.summary: The completed normal Tweester copy supplies zero gap, already proved for either internal floor result. Transporting the enemy does not change that checkpoint.

situations.title: Yes, the desert has swimming offsets
situations.effect: Entering water or hitting its height limits can move Mario's movement position. Swimming pitch and surface bobbing can then add an offset to the stored display after the swimming copy.
situations.prerequisite: A water box and the right swimming action.
situations.area1: The oasis is real: water box 0 covers X -6911..-4223 and Z -7167..-4607, at Y=-127. We cannot cross swimming off just because this is a desert.
situations.timing: An offset while swimming is not yet a raised display beside the pyramid warp. It has to survive leaving the water and everything done afterward.
situations.evidence: The stock water box and swimming writers are identified in the source. No complete oasis-to-Ink transfer is proved.
situations.missing: Show how a legal swimming sequence leaves a useful offset after the exit, or rule out a precisely stated transfer.

gap.amount: About +208 in the generous one-refresh calculation at Y=768
gap.verdict: Insufficient in the checked expression envelope
gap.detail: Pitch adds up to 60. Reset-derived bob height is at most 147.99609375 over every signed-16 reset pitch. Granting both maxima independently after one copy at actual Y=768 gives display Y=975.99609375, a gap of 207.99609375. That is still 962.868774 below the supplied display.
gap.limit: This finite expression envelope uses the unchanged stock sine table and reset-derived bob state. It is not a reachable swim maximum or a bound on extra calls without a fresh copy. Entry/exit height clamps and support changes are separate writes.

review.summary: The checked single-refresh pitch/bob expression is below 208 units, even granting independent maxima. The oasis is distant; a separate clamp or later downward move would need its own case.

situations.title: The oasis does not come with a whirlpool
situations.effect: The whirlpool action changes Mario's movement position and updates display.
situations.prerequisite: A whirlpool object and its matching interaction and action.
situations.area1: The checked stock SSL lists do not select a whirlpool. Having water does not supply one.
situations.timing: Ordinary swimming and whirlpool capture are different mechanisms.
situations.evidence: The US/JP stock-list exclusion is proved. We keep the separate swimming case open where it belongs.
situations.missing: The stock-whirlpool explanation is done. A claim about every action history would also have to rule out an illegitimate way into the whirlpool action.

proof.claim: The checked stock SSL lists cannot select the whirlpool behavior.
proof.scope: Both US and JP; regular script choices and the checked Area-1 macro and special-object lists. This excludes these stock selections, not every possible later object-creation history.

situations.title: The shell gives Mario a display offset
situations.status: Insufficient alone · source review + finite check
situations.effect: Shell riding updates the display and adds a riding or tilting offset. In the airborne action, the code adds 42 to display Y.
situations.prerequisite: A Koopa shell and the corresponding riding action.
situations.area1: Yes. The stock shell box is at (5840,940,2500).
situations.timing: Ground and air movement refresh before adding 45 or 42, including wall-stop and in-step missing-floor results. A canceled action adds no shell offset. Later non-shell writers need separate analysis.
situations.evidence: The normal copy and local source-shape proofs remain scoped. The shell branch diagnostic passes 7760 supplied outcome/height cases and their repeated calls in each US/JP build, plus two early exits. It uses explicit helper test doubles, not live terrain or controller histories.
situations.missing: A shell-assisted route still needs a separate downward State writer: at the fixed anchor, another 1125.864868 units after a ground offset. Prove its live helpers, timing and contact before promoting the whole case.

gap.amount: +42 airborne; +45 on the ground, per ordinary refresh
gap.verdict: Insufficient alone — source arithmetic
gap.detail: At actual Y=768, the shell leaves display Y=810 in air or 813 on the ground. Wall results still pass through the step copy; early A/Z returns add nothing. The native helper-outcome diagnostic found no stacking. See the shell-gap investigation for water, quicksand, speed, mounting and later-writer distinctions.
gap.limit: No shell-specific amplifier was found. This is not a universal bound on shell-assisted histories: another support, dialog or later State write could enlarge a retained small offset, and still needs a concrete useful continuation.
gap.basis: Existing scoped proofs + source review + finite native branch diagnostic

review.summary: Walls do not stack the 42/45-unit shell offset. Keep this scoped insufficiency separate from a later non-shell drop; this batch adds no Coq closure.

situations.title: Negative depth plus a dialog that keeps the display
situations.effect: Sinking subtracts quicksand depth from display Y. If that depth is negative, the subtraction raises the display instead. Skipping a later refresh can keep it there.
situations.prerequisite: A useful negative seed, a collectible reward and the right milestone dialog.
situations.area1: SSL has quicksand and rewards. That does not prove a no-A negative seed. For the agreed transfer test, we may grant the seed and a valid coin/star opportunity.
situations.timing: A dialog can preserve the display, but the warp interaction and remembered platform still have their own checks. We already know that some conditional continuations move Mario while the display survives.
situations.evidence: There are conditional seed-to-A proofs, entry-reset proofs, copy proofs and finite dialog trials. None supplies the whole useful combination of floor loss, contact and top timing.
situations.missing: Build a specific predecessor with the high display, low collision record and first floor miss together. Granting that combination would assume the gameplay result we want.

gap.amount: Display increases by −depth per subtraction when depth is negative
gap.verdict: Large enough arithmetically; the useful producer remains open
gap.detail: A single depth of −1,170.8648681640625 takes a reset display of 768 exactly to the supplied height in binary32. That is a sizing example, not a stock reachable depth. Existing checked arithmetic also gets from supported Y=1280 to 1939 with 1,318 uninterrupted subtractions of depth −0.5.
gap.limit: The small-seed example still needs a 512-unit actual-position drop with display retained. The real reward/dialog sequence and a no-A seed remain unproved. A granted negative seed is not a grant of arbitrary magnitude or of the useful combined setup.
gap.basis: Existing Coq subtraction/iteration results + arithmetic witness

review.summary: Negative depth can raise display arithmetically. The grant permits a transfer test, not arbitrary depth magnitude, a useful floor loss or a clean no-A seed.

situations.title: A dialog can keep a gap; it cannot create one by pausing
situations.status: Helper · needs an earlier height gap
situations.effect: Some dialog states skip ordinary movement or display refresh. Reading a sign can also move Mario while aligning him with the sign.
situations.prerequisite: A particular sign, NPC or reward dialog, at the right action and timer.
situations.area1: Signs and Bob-omb Buddy are present. The automatic milestone dialog is a separate reward-dependent case.
situations.timing: Pausing keeps what was already there. On release, the next action or floor check decides whether that old gap is useful.
situations.evidence: The dialog gate and particular post-dialog refreshes are proved. We cannot treat every dialog as the same kind of freeze.
situations.missing: Find the last position change before the pause and the first useful check afterward, including the floor and contact checks.

gap.amount: No independent fixed upward offset; preserves what enters
gap.verdict: A possible keeper, not the original height source
gap.detail: Automatic dialog can leave the stored display untouched. Repeated sand subtraction belongs in the sand row. Ordinary sign alignment moves X/Z and then copies display; NPC dialog also has a display copy.
gap.limit: We need the particular dialog branch and release boundary. We do not assume every dialog preserves a gap. Active automatic dialog also skips the warp handler.

review.summary: A pause may keep an existing display. The sand subtraction, if any, supplies the height and is counted separately.

situations.title: Bringing a gap through a warp or level entry
situations.effect: Entry and warp code can relocate or reset positions. Door actions have their own movement and animation copies.
situations.prerequisite: The particular warp or level command and a legitimate way of reaching it.
situations.area1: SSL has ordinary fading and nonfading warps. Area 1 has no instant-warp command, and the named door actions are not its stock entrance mechanism.
situations.timing: Our checkpoint is before the disappearing action and Area-2 initialization. A change after that point cannot explain a gap already present when the warp was accepted.
situations.evidence: The reached entry-depth reset and real warp-call connection are proved. The accepted-warp final action call also preserves the positions it receives. Earlier calls have separate limits.
situations.missing: A gap or actor brought from another course must survive the real transition. We cannot carry it across by assumption.

gap.amount: Instant warp: incoming gap − vertical warp displacement
gap.verdict: Relocation can make a gap elsewhere; no matching Area-1 table
gap.detail: The instant-warp code moves State and raw collision, leaving stored display for later work. A downward displacement could therefore create the right sign. The stock SSL script supplies no Area-1 instant warp; its Area-2/3 instant warps have zero displacement. The upper object-warp's proved final action tail creates no new split.
gap.limit: This is a stock-script/source distinction, not a theorem about every imported state. A normal area entry and door sequence need their own copies traced; changes after the selected acceptance checkpoint are too late.
gap.basis: Pinned script and source review + existing acceptance-tail proof

review.summary: Area 1 has no stock instant-warp table. The Area-2/3 instant warps displace by zero and occur after our checkpoint. Ordinary warp-entry and imported-state histories remain separate.

situations.title: Butterflies: this stock list cannot supply the unusual writer
situations.effect: A butterfly briefly adds to Mario's raw collision coordinates to calculate its aim, then subtracts afterward. Those coordinates are being used as temporary working space.
situations.prerequisite: A live butterfly running that helper.
situations.area1: The checked US/JP Area-1 stock lists do not select butterflies.
situations.timing: Adding and subtracting floating-point numbers is not automatically an exact undo. We also do not get to invent a collision check between those operations.
situations.evidence: The unusual raw-position writer and the stock-list exclusion are already checked.
situations.missing: The normal stock-list explanation is finished. A wider claim still needs to establish which callbacks and object records can actually be used during gameplay.

proof.claim: The checked stock Area-1 lists cannot select butterflies.
proof.scope: Both US and JP; regular script choices and the checked Area-1 macro and special-object lists. This excludes these stock selections, not every possible later object-creation history.

situations.title: Ending cutscenes can place Mario almost wherever they need him
situations.status: Different context · not a stock SSL entry
situations.effect: The ending and jumbo-star sequences deliberately move Mario or his stored display to stage the scene.
situations.prerequisite: The proper endgame actions and the code that starts them.
situations.area1: The ending sequence is not an ordinary SSL entry or reward dance. SSL's actual dialogs and rewards have their own entries in this catalog.
situations.timing: Finding a function in the executable does not show that SSL can start that action.
situations.evidence: The generated position-write scan finds these assignments, so we have kept them visible rather than silently dropping them.
situations.missing: A full gameplay proof must check the real action constructors. 'All cutscenes are harmless' is not a substitute for doing that.

gap.amount: Depends on the selected ending/door/action sequence
gap.verdict: No legitimate SSL producer established
gap.detail: Some cutscenes relocate movement or display independently. Finding that assignment in the executable does not show an ordinary SSL action can enter the scene. There is no sound universal number for this mixed group.
gap.limit: Identify a legal first action constructor and exact coordinate writer before treating this as a candidate. No arbitrary action selection is granted.
gap.basis: Source review; action entry remains open

review.summary: An ending-scene relocation is not a stock SSL reward or action entry. A legal SSL first constructor would be needed before it becomes a gameplay candidate.

situations.title: Debug free movement is outside this gameplay challenge
situations.effect: The debug action directly moves Mario and refreshes his display.
situations.prerequisite: Entry into the debug action.
situations.area1: A compiled debug helper does not make injected debug actions an ordinary controller route through SSL.
situations.timing: Choosing an arbitrary action value is outside the model used for this challenge.
situations.evidence: The source scan keeps the function on the list, marked as outside scope. That is a scope choice, not a new impossibility proof.
situations.missing: A study of debug builds or injected actions would need different rules. This catalog does not include that study.

gap.amount: 0 at its display copy; arbitrary entry is outside this challenge
gap.verdict: No authorized stock-gameplay producer
gap.detail: The debug movement action copies its result into display. Choosing this action by changing game state is not controller-driven gameplay under the selected rules.
gap.limit: This is a scope decision, not a proof that all normal action transitions are covered.

review.summary: Injected debug-action entry is outside this controller-gameplay task. Listing its code does not make a new route.

situations.title: Looking displaced is not always a change to the stored display
situations.effect: The camera, mirror proxy, object transforms and temporary vectors can all have something called pos. A write to one of those is not automatically a write to Mario's three relevant positions.
situations.prerequisite: We have to identify the actual object or local variable receiving the write.
situations.area1: Camera and rendering code are present. The castle mirror proxy is another object, not another live Mario slot.
situations.timing: A visual animation or matrix shift only helps the retry if it changes the particular stored vector that the retry reads.
situations.evidence: The broad scan deliberately catches harmless lookalikes, including a coin-formation local vector and camera bookkeeping. They are accounted for here.
situations.missing: Where a proof depends on one of these being separate from Mario, prove that actual storage relationship. Do not classify by the name pos alone.

gap.amount: 0 from writes only to camera, proxy, matrix or local vectors
gap.verdict: No gap unless the actual stored display vector changes
gap.detail: A drawn or camera-relative movement does not help the retry if the stored Mario display position stays put. The mirror uses its own object; local vectors and transforms must be distinguished from Mario's cells.
gap.limit: Actual receivers and aliases still matter. This is not permission to treat every renderer or animation call as harmless.

review.summary: Moving the camera, a mirror proxy or a draw matrix does not change the stored display used by the retry. A genuine write to Mario would need to be identified separately.

situations.title: A helper moves its object. Which object is that?
situations.status: Ownership coverage · not a sized producer
situations.effect: Movement helpers and behavior commands write to the object they receive. The allocator initializes the slot it returns.
situations.prerequisite: A real call, its actual destination and valid Object-pool ownership.
situations.area1: SSL runs many of these helpers. A spawned child here is another object, such as a particle; it does not mean another Mario.
situations.timing: Two objects can occupy different slots in the same pool. The proof must show that the writes stay in the intended slot.
situations.evidence: The particle-copy and allocator proofs settle specific calls and initialization steps. The full sequence of callbacks and object lifetimes is still open.
situations.missing: For the remaining calls in the chosen interval, identify the real destination and its writes. Arbitrary pointer modification is outside the gameplay rules.

gap.amount: No common numeric bound; depends on the actual receiver
gap.verdict: Known distinct-child copies add 0 to Mario; wider coverage remains open
gap.detail: The completed copy into a different valid particle slot preserves Mario. A generic position helper acting on Mario instead would need its own argument and write analysis. Existing stock graphical-offset command payloads are at most +240 even if granted to Mario, but that does not cover every generic write.
gap.limit: The allocator/child theorems keep their stated boundaries. Ownership, other callbacks and alias coverage are not replaced with a blanket zero-gap assumption.
gap.basis: Existing local proofs and command census

review.summary: This is a coverage question, not one measured gap producer. Distinct-child copies preserve Mario in the existing local proofs; other actual receivers still need checking.

situations.title: A skipped update needs something worth preserving
situations.status: Helper · needs an earlier height gap
situations.effect: The ordinary movement-to-Object copy brings collision up to date. A skipped phase may preserve an old mismatch, but skipping alone does not move Mario.
situations.prerequisite: The actual update order, action return, time-stop flags and copy destination.
situations.area1: All of this matters in SSL. The initialized second-State-copy proposal is already excluded in the existing source model.
situations.timing: Even an early return from execute_mario_action goes back to Mario's object update, which then performs the ordinary copy. A skipped-copy proposal must show what really bypasses it.
situations.evidence: The copy-index and completed-copy results are checked. That does not yet prove the scheduler and object identity for every possible history.
situations.missing: Pair a real position change with an actual delayed or skipped copy, then reach the contact or floor query before the advantage disappears.

gap.amount: No new display-minus-movement gap; collision copy transfers an existing one
gap.verdict: Can complete the low collision record only after a producer exists
gap.detail: If actual Mario has already moved down while display stayed high, copying State into the raw Object makes collision low too. That is useful bookkeeping for Ink, but it does not create the original height difference. Skipping a phase merely preserves its incoming values.
gap.limit: The crucial order is whether that collision copy happens before another display refresh. The ordinary caller still copies State after execute_mario_action returns.

review.summary: A collision copy can make an already-low actual position available to contact. A skipped update preserves values; neither supplies the earlier height change.

situations.title: A different floor answer is not itself a position write
situations.status: Helper · needs an earlier height gap
situations.effect: A signed-16 conversion or a different sample point can give a different floor answer without writing any of Mario's three position records.
situations.prerequisite: The actual converted coordinates, floor lists and query point.
situations.area1: SSL uses this collision code too. Useful distant coordinates still need a legal way to reach them and make contact.
situations.timing: This can affect how a gap is used. It does not create the gap by itself.
situations.evidence: The finite geometry and coordinate-alias checks keep their stated ranges. They are not a proof about every controller history.
situations.missing: Connect a reachable pose to the live floor choice and accepted warp contact. Memory corruption is not part of this mechanism.

gap.amount: 0 new position gap
gap.verdict: Changes what a query sees, not where the records are
gap.detail: Signed-16 conversion can make the floor query see different coordinates. It does not itself write State, display or raw collision. It may help use a separately created gap.
gap.limit: A changed floor answer can feed a later snap or retry, which belongs to that writer's row. Ordinary coordinates are used by the supplied vertical setup.

review.summary: Coordinate conversion changes the query input, not the three stored positions. A resulting snap or retry is counted under its actual writer.

gapReview.note: Size the display-minus-movement gap before the first floor query. After the retry, movement can agree with display while raw collision stays low. This sizing pass does not attempt the transfer to the warp.

gapReviewGroups.title: Concrete producer still open
gapReviewGroups.explanation: Four mechanisms can write height in the useful direction. Their reachable size and surviving copies still need checking.

gapReviewGroups.title: Insufficient at the stated checkpoint
gapReviewGroups.explanation: Six scoped cases fall short. Two have Coq execution proofs; four retain source or finite-calculation evidence. Other exits and combinations are separate.

gapReviewGroups.title: Helper, not a height source
gapReviewGroups.explanation: Five mechanisms can preserve, transfer or use an existing gap. Do not count them as five independent ways to create the height difference.

gapReviewGroups.title: No local stock producer identified
gapReviewGroups.explanation: Four entries describe absent local ingredients, other scenes, excluded debug entry or the wrong position record. Their exact source and scope limits remain attached.

gapReviewGroups.title: Which object is being written?
gapReviewGroups.explanation: One entry collects receiver and callback coverage. A particle moving is not Mario moving; any exception needs an actual Mario receiver.
